Attached is the working April KPI snapshot (april-kpi-dashboard-v3) and a couple supporting artifacts (latency-sample-traces.zip). High level items for QBR prep:

- Overall usage up ~18% month-over-month driven by a handful of mid-market customers; cost is up ~12% and margins tighten if we don’t optimize batching/quant.
- P95 latency: trending +40ms in EU over last 72h; initial signals point to model variant quant3 rollout on dedicated pools.
- Uptime: 99.95% platform-wide, but we saw a 23-minute blip on 4/8 in eu-west; investigating whether autoscaler timing was a factor.

Asking: please review the dashboard before EOD today and call out any items you want explicitly surfaced in the QBR deck (econ impact, mitigation plan, or owner). Specific requests:
- Laura: can you confirm customer-impact (any escalations) and give a short one-liner we can use in the slide?

- Rishi: cost delta by model + 7d trend (can you attach the latest sheet).
- Lauren + Evelyn: confirm ops SLO / incident timeline and note any outstanding postmortem items.

I’ll consolidate into the QBR deck tonight and share a draft by 08:00 PT tomorrow.

Quick read of the traces — two observations:

1) The latency bump coincides with the quant3 rollout we pushed to dedicated pools on 4/6. quant3 reduces GPU memory but increases attention kernel hops for certain seq-lengths (esp. >512). The affected customers have longer context averages.
2) The autoscaler logs show several delayed scale-ups in eu-west yesterday (see OPS-3241), which could amplify the P95.

Recommendation:
- Immediate: add a routing policy to divert 10% of traffic from dedicated eu-west to hosted eu-backup for those customer routes (canary for 24h).
- Short term: revert the quant3 rollout for dedicated pools and run quant3-only experiments on a canary subset.
- Ask: Rishi, can you provide an estimated cost impact of diverting 10% traffic for 24/48h (ballpark) so leadership can weigh the tradeoff?

I can own the rollback plan with infra help.

—Markus
Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attaching cost-by-model-Q1.xlsx with the short tables. Quick summary:

- Diverting 10% of EU dedicated traffic to hosted eu-backup for 24h is ~+$9k incremental cost (compute + egress), 48h ~+$16k.
- The quant3 variant currently saves ~18% token cost on average for small/medium contexts, but for long-context customers we see +12% latency P95 with little cost benefit.
- If we rollback quant3 on dedicated eu pools we should expect a ~+$6k/day cost increase versus keeping quant3 (because of slightly higher mem usage), but latency recovers ~30-45ms at P95.
